Hi Priya / Silvershore network team,

Thanks for the call this morning. Per our discussion here is the minimal provisioning checklist Redwood needs to stand up the private deployment in your VPC / on-prem edge: 

- AWS/GCP account numbers or on-prem connectivity owner
- Service account (JSON) with: compute.admin (or equivalent), iam.serviceAccounts.actAs, storage.read
- Interconnect details: IP ranges for BGP, public egress IPs for allowlisting (if applicable)
- Subnet plan (AZs, CIDR blocks, preferred MTU)
- KMS key ARN (or HSM vendor contact) and key policy for customer-managed keys
- Expected peak concurrency, target p95 latency SLO, and retention window for audit logs
- Firewall rules: outbound ports 443, 80; intra-VPC ports 2200, 5000-5010 (for runtime control plane)

Attached: topology sketch (silvershore-architecture-mtap.pdf) and a baseline subnet plan. Can you confirm the service account and the subnet/CIDR matrix by EOD Tue (2026-07-13)? Once we have those we’ll queue the IAM and VPC peering tasks and schedule the staging smoke test.

Thanks —
Marcus

Priya — great, thanks for the fast turnaround and the subnet sheet. Short answers: 

- MTU: Redwood runtime can operate with MTU=9000 but we recommend validating end-to-end (load balancers and any transit appliance). If you choose jumbo frames, we’ll include MTU checks in our smoke test.
- Audit logs: for SOC2 evidence we typically ask for 90 days of CloudTrail-level events and 365 days for ELB/access logs if possible; minimum ingest we need: control plane calls (create/update/delete), auth events, and token issuance events. If retention is an issue we can work a reduced window for the pilot.

Next steps I’m taking on our side:
1) I’ll open the deployment ticket and request the service account JSON securely.
2) Hannah will draft a staging validation runbook (network tests, cert install, KMS sign/verify) and share by tomorrow.
3) Marcus will book the staging smoke test slot for Thu (7/15).

Action items for Silvershore: confirm SA share method, confirm BGP ticket owner and a contact for HSM/KMS policy.

–Lauren

Hi all —

I’ve attached the initial validation runbook and a short preflight script we’ll run on the staging cluster. Highlights / tests included: 

- Connectivity: ping across subnets, MTU validation, DNS resolution for internal control plane FQNs
- Firewall: verify outbound 443 and allowed control ports; test blocked-port behaviour to ensure no open admin ports exposed
- KMS: sign/verify roundtrip using the customer KMS key, and verify key policy logs show our service account operations
- Metrics & Tracing: ensure token issuance is logged and a sample trace crosses from runtime -> control plane -> KMS
- Performance: quick 100-concurrency tokenized run to validate p95 under pilot capacity

Please review the runbook and call out any additional tests you require for compliance. I’ll run the preflight at 09:00 on 2026-07-15 and share results in this thread.
